facts.statement: The genus Nanshiungosaurus was described by Dong Zhiming in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Dong, 1979

facts.statement: The type species Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus was discovered in 1974 and formally described in 1979.
facts.quote: The type species, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, was first discovered in 1974 and described in 1979 by Dong Zhiming.

facts.statement: A second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was described in 1997 based on remains found in 1992, but its validity is unsupported.
facts.quote: A supposed and unlikely second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was found in 1992 and described in 1997.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Nanshiungosaurus were discovered in 1974 during an expedition at the Nanxiong Basin in Guangdong Province.
facts.quote: In 1974, during a geological expedition at the Nanxiong Basin led by the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology several fossilized remains of dinosaurs were discovered by the team.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (IVPP V4731) consists of 12 cervical, 10 dorsal, 6 sacral, and the first caudal vertebrae along with a nearly complete pelvis.
facts.quote: The specimen was labelled under the number IVPP V4731 and consisted of 12 cervical (lacking the atlas), 10 dorsal, 5 (actually 6) sacral and the first caudal vertebrae with a nearly complete, bulky pelvis only lacking the right ilium and ischium.

facts.statement: The genus name Nanshiungosaurus refers to Nanxiong city and is derived from the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Nanshiungosaurus, refers to the site of provenance Nanxiong city and is derived from the Greek σαῦρος (sauros, meaning lizard).

facts.statement: The species name brevispinus means 'short spine' in Latin, referring to the relatively short vertebral spines.
facts.quote: Lastly, the specific name, brevispinus, is derived from the Latin brevis and spina (meaning short and spine, respectively) in reference to the relatively short vertebral spines.

facts.statement: A second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was named in 1997 based on a skeleton found near Mazongshan in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1997 Dong Zhiming and You Hailu named and described a supposed second species: "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, based on a skeleton found in 1992 near Mazongshan.

facts.statement: In 2010, Lindsay Zanno argued that "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini is unrelated to the main genus and might warrant its own genus due to its different age and lack of shared characteristics.
facts.quote: In 2010, the North American paleontologist Lindsay Zanno considered this referral to be highly improbable since "N". bohlini dates back from the Barremian-Aptian ages and in the view of lack of synapomorphies, she considered that the supposed second species is unrelated to Nanshiungosaurus and might warrant its own genus.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus was a therizinosaurid dinosaur that lived in South China during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus (meaning "Nanxiong's lizard") is a genus of therizinosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now South China during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus was a large therizinosaurid estimated to reach nearly 5 meters in length and weigh between 600 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a large-sized therizinosaurid that is estimated to have reached nearly 5 m in length and to have weighed about 600 - 907 kg.

facts.statement: Early research on therizinosaurs was complicated by sparse remains that led some to interpret them as prosauropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: At first, the research on therizinosaurs was complicated since sparse remains were known at the time and these had features from multiple dinosaur lineages leading to their interpretation as prosauropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The unusual pelvic shape initially led the describer to think it was a dwarf sauropod, but it was later recognized as a therizinosaur based on similarities with Segnosaurus.
facts.quote: The unusual shape of the pelvis led Dong, the original describer, to interpret the remains as belonging to a dwarf sauropod, but during the 1990s the genus was recognized as a segnosaur (now therizinosaur) based on the pelvic similarities with Segnosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus is differentiated by stocky posterior cervical vertebrae with opisthocoel (concave posterior) centra.
facts.quote: This taxon can be differentiated by the possession of stocky posterior-most cervical vertebrae with opisthocoel (meaning that they were concave on their posterior sides) centra.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus was a pot-bellied animal with a strong build, stout hindlimbs, and a functionally four-toed foot.
facts.quote: Like other derived (advanced) therizinosaurids, Nanshiungosaurus was a pot-bellied animal that had a strong build composed of stout hindlimbs with a functionally tetradactyl pes.

facts.statement: The arms of Nanshiungosaurus ended in large, recurved claws that were flattened from side to side.
facts.quote: The arms ended up in large, recurved claws that were side to side flattened.

facts.statement: Although the holotype lacks a skull, related therizinosaurids suggest Nanshiungosaurus had a small skull with coarsely serrated teeth and a prominent keratinous beak.
facts.quote: Though the holotype specimen lacks cranial material, the preserved elements in therizinosaurids Erlikosaurus and Segnosaurus indicate that it had a relatively small skull with coarsely serrated teeth, and developed a prominent rhamphotheca (keratinous beak).

facts.statement: The well-preserved axis vertebra measures 13.5 cm in length and has platycoelus (slightly concave at both ends) centra.
facts.quote: The axis is well preserved and has a length of 13.5 cm with platycoelus (slightly concave at both ends) centra.

facts.statement: The seventh and eighth cervical vertebrae are the longest, with centra measuring 18 cm in length.
facts.quote: Seventh and eighth cervicals are the longest with 18 cm long centra and posterior to them, the vertebral size slightly narrows.

facts.statement: Dorsal vertebrae centra are narrow, platycoelous, and have an average length of 7 cm.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae centra, unlike in the cervicals, are narrow and platycoelous with an average length of 7 cm.

facts.statement: Dorsal vertebrae are pneumatic with shallow pits on the lateral sides, though these features reduce in size on posterior dorsals.
facts.quote: They are also pneumatic with shallow pneumatopores (pits leading to air pockets) on the lateral sides, but they reduce in size on posterior dorsals.

facts.statement: In most dorsal vertebrae, the neural spines are very elongated, stocky, side-to-side thickened, and topped with stout tuberosities.
facts.quote: In most dorsals, the neural spines are very elongated, the articular processes are located within the ligaments of the centrum, the neural spines are stocky, side to side thickened, and the top regions have stout tuberosities.

facts.statement: The sacrum consists of six fused sacral vertebrae, indicating the individual was an adult when it died.
facts.quote: The sacrum is composed by six (originally five) sacral vertebrae and they are fused into a single structure, indicating that the individual was an adult at the time of death.

facts.statement: It is debated whether "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini belongs to the genus, as the original describers provided no evidence or argumentation to support the assignment.
facts.quote: Dong and Yu presented no evidence or argumentation supporting the assignment of the species to Nanshiungosaurus.

facts.statement: There is a scientific consensus that the specimen "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini is no longer considered related to the main genus Nanshiungosaurus.
facts.quote: As an overall consensus, this dubious specimen is no longer considered to be relatable to Nanshiungosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus had an opisthopubic pelvis where the pubis and ischium were fused and directed backwards.
facts.quote: Like other derived therizinosaurids, the pelvis has an opisthopubic condition where the pubis and ischium are fused and directed backwards.

facts.statement: The ilium of Nanshiungosaurus was stocky with an extremely well-developed, elongated preacetabular process but lacked a postacetabular process.
facts.quote: The ilium is stocky with an extremely well-developed and elongated preacetabular process (anterior expansion of the iliac blade), nevertheless, the postacetabular process (posterior expansion) is missing.

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis by Zanno concluded that the family Nanshiungosauridae was invalid and a synonym of Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2010, Zanno performed one of the most complete analyses of the Therizinosauria at that point and noted that these two species do not pertain to the same genus and therefore the use of the Nanshiungosauridae was invalid and represents a synonym of Therizinosauridae.

facts.statement: Most cladistic analyses support the classification of Nanshiungosaurus as a therizinosaurid.
facts.quote: The therizinosaurid placement of Nanshiungosaurus has been widely followed and corroborated by most cladistic analyses.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus was discovered in 1974 and formally described in 1979 based on a specimen preserving most cervical and dorsal vertebrae and the pelvis.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus se descubrió por primera vez en 1974 y se describió en 1979, representada por un espécimen que preserva la mayoría de las vértebras cervicales y dorsales con la pelvis.

facts.statement: A doubtful second species, Nanshiungosaurus bohlini, was found in 1992 and described in 1997.
facts.quote: Una supuesta y dudosa segunda especie, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini , fue encontrada en 1992 y descrita en 1997.

facts.statement: The holotype of Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus preserves most cervical and dorsal vertebrae along with the pelvis.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus se descubrió por primera vez en 1974 y se describió en 1979, representada por un espécimen que preserva la mayoría de las vértebras cervicales y dorsales con la pelvis.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus was estimated to be 4.4 to 5 meters long and weigh between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus era un terizinosaurio de cuerpo relativamente grande, estimado en 4,4 a 5 metros de largo con un peso de 454 a 907 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The species Nanshiungosaurus bohlini was estimated by Paul to be 6 meters long and weigh 1.3 tonnes, distinguished by fused cervical ribs.
facts.quote: "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini es un poco más grande, estimado por Paul en 6 metros y 1,3 toneladas, sus vértebras eran únicas, con las costillas cervicales fusionadas que lo distinguía de Alxasaurus.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus is distinguished by having twelve robust cervical vertebrae with opistocoelic centers, meaning they were concave on their posterior sides.
facts.quote: N. brevispinus se distingue por la posesión de doce vértebras cervicales robustas con centros vertebrales opistocoelicos, lo que significa que eran cóncavas en sus lados posteriores.

facts.statement: The number of sacral vertebrae in Nanshiungosaurus was initially determined to be five but was later corrected to six.
facts.quote: El número de vértebras sacras se determinó primero en cinco, luego se corrigió a seis.

facts.statement: The fused sacral vertebrae indicate that the Nanshiungosaurus individual was an adult at the time of death.
facts.quote: Las vértebras sacras están fusionadas, lo que indica que el individuo era un adulto en el momento de la muerte.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus was one of the last therizinosaurids to exist.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus was one of the last therizinosaurs to exist.

facts.statement: Fossils of Nanshiungosaurus were found in the Nanxiong Formation, dated to about 66.7 ± 0.3 million years ago in the latest Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: The fossil remains were unearthed from the Nanxiong Formation, which has been dated to the latest Maastrichtian stage about 66.7 ± 0.3 million years ago.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus was a bulky high-browser that shared its habitat with various oviraptorosaur species.
facts.quote: The therizinosaurid Nanshiungosaurus was a bulky high-browser in its ecosystem, and shared its habitat with multiple oviraptorosaur species such as Banji, Ganzhousaurus, Corythoraptor, Nankangia, Huanansaurus or Shixinggia.

facts.statement: The ecosystem of Nanshiungosaurus included the tyrannosaurid Qianzhousaurus, the sauropod Gannansaurus, and sparse remains of the hadrosaurid Microhadrosaurus.
facts.quote: Additional dinosaurs are represented by the fast-running, long-snouted tyrannosaurid Qianzhousaurus, the sauropod Gannansaurus, and the very sparse remains of hadrosaurid dinosaurs such as Microhadrosaurus (now a nomen dubium).

facts.statement: The fauna of Nanshiungosaurus included nanhsiungchelyid turtles, squamates like Chianghsia and Tianyusaurus, and the crocodilian Jiangxisuchus.
facts.quote: Other reptiles that composed the fauna were the terrestrial or semiaquatic nanhsiungchelyid turtles Nanhsiungchelys and Jiangxichelys, squamates Chianghsia and Tianyusaurus, and the crocodilian Jiangxisuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nanshiungosaurus bohlini belongs to the genus due to significant age differences from the type species and issues with authentic characteristics.
facts.quote: También conserva las vértebras, pero esta especie, sin embargo, tiene una gran diferencia de edad en comparación con la especie tipo y problemas relacionados con las características auténticas, lo que hace que su asignación al género sea cuestionable.

facts.statement: The first remains of Nanshiungosaurus were collected in 1974 by an expedition team from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Nanshiungosaurus fueron recolectados en 1974 por un equipo de expedición del Instituto de Paleontología y Paleoantropología de Vertebrados.

facts.statement: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus was named and described by Dong Zhiming in 1979.
facts.quote: Más tarde, en 1979, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus fue nombrado y descrito por Dong Zhiming.

facts.statement: The generic name refers to Nanxiong, while the specific name derives from Latin for 'short' and 'spine', referencing short vertebral spines.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se refiere a Nanxiong y el nombre específico se deriva del latín brevis, "corto" y spina, "espina", en referencia a las espinas vertebrales cortas.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull but including 12 cervical, 10 dorsal, and 6 sacral vertebrae, plus a voluminous pelvis.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo pero que incluye 12 vértebras cervicales, 10 dorsales y 6 sacras y una pelvis voluminosa.

facts.statement: It was initially thought to be a small, strange sauropod characterized by a shorter but thicker neck than other sauropods.
facts.quote: Primero se pensó que era un saurópodo pequeño y extraño caracterizado por un cuello más corto pero más grueso que otros saurópodos.

facts.statement: In 1997, Dong Zhiming and Yu Hailu named and described a second species, Nanshiungosaurus bohlini, based on a skeleton found in 1992 near Mazongshan.
facts.quote: En 1997, Dong Zhiming y Yu Hailu nombraron y describieron una segunda especie, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, basada en un esqueleto encontrado en 1992 cerca de Mazongshan.

facts.statement: The holotype is IVPP V11116, from the Upper Xinminbao Group of the Early Cretaceous, dating from the Barremian to Aptian.
facts.quote: El holotipo es IVPP V11116, del Grupo del Xinminbao Superior del Cretácico temprano que data del Barremiense al Aptiense.

facts.statement: Dong and Yu provided no evidence or argumentation to support the assignment of the species to Nanshiungosaurus.
facts.quote: Dong y Yu no presentaron evidencia o argumentación que respalden la asignación de la especie a Nanshiungosaurus.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of shared unique traits and the large age difference with Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, the supposed second species is generally considered unrelated and could justify its own genus.
facts.quote: En vista de la falta de sinapomorfias, rasgos únicos compartidos y la gran diferencia de edad con Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, generalmente se considera que la supuesta segunda especie no está relacionada con la posterior y podría justificar su propio género.

facts.statement: In 1979, Dong assigned Nanshiungosaurus to Titanosaurinae based on the assumption that it was a sauropod.
facts.quote: Nanshiungosaurus fue en 1979 por Dong asignado a Titanosaurinae, con base en la suposición de que era un saurópodo.

facts.statement: In 1992, the species was assigned to Segnosauridae, the group now called Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: En 1992 la especie fue asignada a los Segnosauridae, el grupo hoy llamado Therizinosauridae.

facts.statement: However, in 1997, Dong placed N. brevispinus and "N." bohlini in a separate Nanshungosauridae, which is now obsolete.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1997, Dong colocó N. brevispinus y "N". bohlini en un separado Nanshungosauridae, ahora obsoleto.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses indicate a position for Nanshiungosaurus that is basal in Therizinosauridae or just outside that clade, basal in Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Los análisis cladísticos indican una posición para Nanshiungosaurus que es basal en Therizinosauridae o justo fuera de ese clado, basal en Therizinosauroidea.

facts.statement: Under the definition of Therizinosauridae according to Xu in 2002, Nanshiungosaurus is by definition a therizinosaurid.
facts.quote: Bajo la definición de Therizinosauridae según Xu en 2002, Nanshuingosaurus es por definición un terizinosáurido.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Hartman et al. in 2019 recovers Nanshiungosaurus as a therizinosaurid in a more derived position than Erliansaurus or Neimongosaurus.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético realizado por Hartaman et al. en 2019 recupera Nanshiungosaurus como un terizinosáurido en una posición más derivada que Erliansaurus o Neimongosaurus.
